subtopics.title: What Oral History Is and Why It Matters

questions.question: Oral history is:
options: Collecting people's memories of the past through recorded interviews

questions.question: A person describing their own experience of an event gives:
Which of these is a secondary source?
options: A photograph taken during a forced removal

questions.question: Why is oral history especially valuable for studying apartheid?
options: Apartheid left no written records at all
Many ordinary people's experiences were never written down in official records
Oral history is always more accurate than documents

subtopics.title: Choosing and Researching an Apartheid Law

questions.question: Which law classified every South African into a racial group?
options: The Reservation of Separate Amenities Act

questions.question: The Group Areas Act of 1950:
options: Set aside separate residential areas for each racial group

questions.question: The Reservation of Separate Amenities Act of 1953 segregated:
options: Public facilities such as beaches, buses and parks

questions.question: Why should you record the details of every written source you use?
options: So you can reference your sources and avoid plagiarism
So you can copy them word for word

subtopics.title: Planning and Conducting an Ethical Interview

questions.question: Informed consent means the interviewee:
options: Agrees to take part after understanding how the interview will be used

questions.question: Which is an open question?
options: What do you remember about the day your family moved?

questions.question: "Weren't you angry?" is an example of:
What should you do if an interviewee becomes upset?
options: Offer to pause or stop, and respect their wishes

subtopics.title: Evaluating Evidence and Writing Up, and the Error Museum

questions.question: Corroboration means:
options: Checking a source against other evidence that supports it

questions.question: Plagiarism is:
options: Presenting someone else's work as your own

questions.question: Which statement is correct?
options: Oral history is just stories and is not evidence
If a memory differs from a textbook, the person is lying
Interviewees may choose to remain anonymous
Closed questions always get the best answers

questions.question: Why might an interviewee's memory differ from a textbook?
options: The law may have been enforced differently locally, or memory may have faded

questions.question: A "library with legs" in the Simplifier story is:
options: An older person whose memories hold history

questions.question: When did apartheid end?
Most stories of ordinary people under apartheid:
Before an interview, you should first:
options: Research your chosen law in written sources
Decide what the person will say

questions.question: The pass laws forced black South Africans to:
An interviewee is allowed to:
options: Say no, stay anonymous or stop at any time

questions.question: Why should you start an interview with easy background questions?
options: To help the person relax and set the scene before harder questions
Because the law questions do not matter

questions.question: In the jigsaw picture, your interview is:
options: A missing piece that is not needed
The box the puzzle comes in

questions.question: If an interview and a book disagree, you should:
options: Choose the answer you like best

questions.question: At the end of your report, you should list:
What is the main idea of this lesson?
options: Memories of apartheid become evidence when collected respectfully and checked
